scope: Initial matched development outputs, before subsequent narrow review fixes. One masked model review, not observed human benefit or causal attribution to the skills.

cases.conformance: Both correct only “record” to “records”; order, protected wording, and length remain intact.
cases.fidelity: Both preserve the transmission condition, interval, and untested outdoor status.
cases.usefulness: Both deliver the requested narrow correction.
cases.defects: A: no material defect. B: no material defect.

cases.conformance: Both improve the reasoning and propose assessing staffing while retaining backlog reduction. A explicitly states the reduction condition; B quantifies the monthly gap.
cases.fidelity: Both correctly reconcile 36 arrivals and 18 closures with the 12-to-30 backlog and decline to substantiate two hires.
cases.usefulness: Both identify decision-relevant unknowns; neither establishes a staffing level without evidence.
cases.defects: A: no material defect. B: no material defect.

cases.conformance: A preserves the passage unchanged; B adjusts sentence rhythm and punctuation while retaining the repeated keeping and exact ending. Both are reasonable responses to improving flow.
cases.fidelity: Both retain the ticket, smudged address, date, and uncertainty without added experience.
cases.usefulness: A preserves the original cadence; B offers a modest alternative. The supplied constraints do not establish an author preference.
cases.defects: A: no material defect. B: no material defect.

cases.conformance: Both retain “idempotent” and explain the stated retry behavior for a novice.
cases.fidelity: Both preserve Ready and the absence of appended records and notifications without adding other effects.
cases.usefulness: B joins the repeated action and resulting state in one causal explanation; A repeats the Ready outcome across adjacent sentences.
cases.defects: A: adjacent sentences repeat the same status effect, a minor issue. B: no material defect.

cases.conformance: Both develop the storage/inquiry distinction and soften the opening without adding empirical support. A marks its further interpretation “Perhaps”; B stays close to the supplied claim.
cases.fidelity: Neither supplies invented anecdotes, evidence, or motives. Both present inquiry as a conceptual distinction consistent with the notes.
cases.usefulness: A offers a possible forward-looking interpretation; B uses a more compact distinction. Neither is clearly required by the task.
cases.defects: A: no material defect. B: “what to do with it” is somewhat broader than the specific next-question distinction, which its final sentence restores.

cases.conformance: Both report the procedure and flag the unsupported claims, but B puts the issue note in a separate user-facing file. A places the flag in the same text as the Methods passage, so it could be mistaken for manuscript content.
cases.fidelity: Both preserve 40 °C and 10 min and accurately identify the missing comparison and unsupported reader instruction. B also explicitly notes the absence of an external source.
cases.usefulness: B supplies clean Methods text plus a separately accessible explanation; A makes the distinction by paragraph but does not clearly separate the deliverable.
cases.defects: A: the issue discussion is embedded in the deliverable text rather than separately presented. B: no material defect.

cases.conformance: Both analyze functions and relationships with separate anchors and realization spans and allow overlapping readings. B explicitly distinguishes intra-paragraph relations from registered paragraph-ID links and records an alternative qualification reading.
cases.fidelity: Both attribute the proposed rule and treat the urgent approval as hypothetical rather than observed. Neither claims a population rate.
cases.usefulness: B makes the scope of the relation coding clearer. Its “instruct” reading of “Consider” is debatable under the catalogue, but is explicitly explained; A’s broader whole-paragraph support span is also defensible.
cases.defects: A: relation descriptions do not identify the catalogue’s paragraph-ID limitation. B: the instruct label may overread a rhetorical invitation as an actionable reader instruction; it is a contestable coding choice, not a factual error.

cases.conformance: Both stay under 45 words, retain retry-safe, and explain the identifier condition and outcomes.
cases.fidelity: Both preserve the new-identifier consequence and prototype-only test scope without adding causes or tests.
cases.usefulness: Both connect the condition to the result clearly; their differences in sentence structure do not establish a material preference.
cases.defects: A: no material defect. B: no material defect.

cases.conformance: Both give a worked revision immediately and explain the choice.
cases.fidelity: Both accurately state 80 of 100 and avoid inventing a baseline or comparator.
cases.usefulness: Both replace vague praise with the count and explain why an evaluative comparison is unsupported; wording differences do not change the lesson requested.
cases.defects: A: no material defect. B: no material defect.

cases.conformance: Both provide the facts and invite an attempt, but each states the central fact as a complete sentence identical to an obvious worked revision. This makes the instruction to wait before showing an answer imperfectly fulfilled.
cases.fidelity: Both accurately provide the count and absence of a comparator, baseline, and additional outcome.
cases.usefulness: Both offer a practice prompt, but a fact list such as “Correct classifications: 80 of 100” would preserve more room for the user to compose the sentence.
cases.defects: A: presents a complete candidate answer before the attempt despite its note. B: presents the same complete candidate answer before the attempt despite its note.

cases.conformance: Both explain cache and synchronization in context within 120 words.
cases.fidelity: Both preserve the five-minute copying interval, displayed source, possible stale value, and latest synchronization timestamp without inventing validation.
cases.usefulness: Both explain how changes between synchronizations can cause a difference; “if” versus “can” is not a material distinction here.
cases.defects: A: no material defect. B: no material defect.

cases.conformance: Both are brief openings under 90 words, retain the exact required sentence, and leave the ending open.
cases.fidelity: Both preserve the closed bakery, six, kitchen light, desire to approach, and uncertainty without added memories or motives.
cases.usefulness: Both form a coherent opening; the paragraph break in B is an aesthetic option rather than evidence of superior voice.
cases.defects: A: no material defect. B: no material defect.

known_limitations: Ten project-known synthetic cases plus two parent-authored drafting cases; one output per arm per case, clustered six per context.
Fresh contexts shared a filesystem and obeyed instructed read boundaries; this was not an OS access-control sandbox.

The revised-B executor disclosed reading all twelve raw task inputs from the shared file despite its six-task assignment. It reported no access to other outputs, verdicts or skills. Extra raw-task exposure weakens strict contextual equivalence; no gold or old output was contained in that file.
Three B preferences under the balanced mask do not rule out position effects.
The comparator assesses delivered formatting/analysis as well as prose. No author acceptance, comprehension, learning transfer or coding accuracy is established.
